title: The complaint: corrected on Monday, repeated on Tuesday
sub: The model is stateless by design. The system around it is what forgets.
caption: Corrected on Monday, repeated on Tuesday: the model is stateless by design, and nothing around it records, selects or measures.
alt: Two chat sessions. On Monday the user says never use the word skyrocket and the assistant agrees. On Tuesday, in a new session with empty context, the assistant uses the word. Three missing things are listed: nothing records the correction in a checkable form, nothing decides which notes shape future answers, nothing measures improvement.

title: Why “store the corrections and inject them” fails
sub: The obvious first design breaks within a month, for five structural reasons.
caption: The naive design: a growing corrections file pasted into every prompt, and the five ways it fails.
alt: A corrections file pasted into every prompt, then five numbered failures: kinds get mixed, facts go stale, text leaks, the list grows, nothing is measured.

title: The learning loop: seven stages, a sign-off at each gate
sub: What moves between stages is a file. What decides is a person. Not a list in a prompt.
caption: The loop: seven rerunnable stages. Every arrow carries a file; every gate has a person.
alt: Record, enrich, group, extract, serve, evaluate and approve form a ring. Each arrow names the file that moves to the next stage and carries a sign-off marker. A dashed arrow returns what failed replay from evaluate to extract.

title: Kinds of learning, and how each one is handled
sub: The taxonomy decides the serving rule. Without it the serving layer cannot tell a fact from a preference.
caption: Five kinds of learning, each with its own serving rule, staleness and position in the package.
alt: A table of five kinds of learning: world fact, method rule, answer shape, profile and standing watch, each with an example in the user's words, how it is served, whether it goes stale and its layer. Below: scope, owner and precedence rules.

title: One correction’s journey through the loop
sub: Monday’s sentence becomes Tuesday’s behaviour, with a file at every step and a person at the gate.
caption: One rule, end to end: from the user's sentence to the next session's behaviour.
alt: Eight steps from a user's sentence on Monday, through record, enrich, group, extract, serve and evaluate, to approval and Tuesday's session starting with the new package.

title: Anatomy of a served item
sub: Every item quotes the user’s own words. A world fact is served as a dated claim to check, never as a fact.
caption: A learning item carries its kind, scope, verbatim quote and source; the rendering differs by kind.
alt: A learning item with kind, scope, verbatim quote, source record and status, each annotated. Two rendered lines: a method rule applied directly, and a world fact rendered as verify before use with its date.

title: A package has a budget and layers
sub: How-to-work first, watches last. Anything cut is listed, never silently dropped.
caption: The package: layered by kind, cut at a budget, with the cut list outside the budget.
alt: A context package drawn as four stacked layers with a budget line cutting through the last layer and a not-included list below. Four notes: position matters, order is a design decision, cuts are listed, stable bytes cache well.

title: Evaluate by replay before anything goes live
sub: Later questions, answered with and without the package, judged blind, measured against what the user actually corrected.
caption: Replay: two arms, a blind judge, code guards, and a pass line on corrections the package never saw.
alt: A time bar splits sessions at a cutoff date: packages are built from the earlier ones, questions come from the later ones. A later question is answered in two arms, as today and with the package; a blind model judge and code guards score both; the verdict is the pass line on later corrections met.

title: Pre-register the test, pin the code, gate each stage
sub: Write the pass line before the run. Hash the code and the prompt. A mismatch refuses the run.
caption: The registration file fixes the test before the run; one person signs off at each stage.
alt: A registration file with hypothesis, pass line, sample, prompt and code hashes and an empty deviations list; a note that a hash mismatch refuses the run. Beside it, seven stages with what the person checks at each sign-off.

title: When this loop is the wrong tool
sub: Build it when corrections are per-user, recur across sessions, and a wrong answer has a cost.
caption: Alternatives compared: where notes, vendor memory, retrieval or fine-tuning are enough, and where the loop earns its cost.
alt: A comparison table of notes in the prompt, a vendor memory tool, retrieval over transcripts, fine-tuning and this loop, across per-user, provenance, staleness, withdrawal, measurement and build cost. Below, when each simpler option is enough.

title: Day 1 and week 1
sub: Make learning checkable first, then provable.
caption: What to build on day 1 and in week 1.
alt: Two checklists. Day 1: record schema, taxonomy enum, verbatim-quote check, verify-then-apply rendering, budget with listed cuts, package stamp on each answer. Week 1: cutoff date, extraction prompt and sample, calibrated judge, registration file, named approvers, withdrawal path and cost ceiling. Closing line: approval is a step, not a hope.
